idiom_name: include Enumerable over a private frozen Array; DelegateClass(Array) when forwarding is wanted
implementation_notes: Ruby's idiom is to mix in a protocol rather than inherit a container: `include Enumerable` plus an #each that yields the elements gives map, select, sort, find, sum and the rest for free, while the backing Array stays an instance variable. Mutators remain explicit methods that re-check the invariants; freezing the stored array (@items.freeze) stops accidental in-place edits from inside the class and gives callers frozen read access, but freeze is shallow and Array-level only - element objects stay mutable and dup/clone return unfrozen copies. When the whole Array surface must be forwarded, build the class with DelegateClass(Array) (or wrap with SimpleDelegator) and undef the mutators you refuse; delegating to a raw Array without that step re-publishes push and << and with them the leak.
pitfalls: Enumerable provides only the read side; every writer you add (<<, push, clear) becomes an invariant-checking entry point that must validate.
freeze is shallow and type-specific: elements stay mutable and dup/clone hand back unfrozen arrays, so frozen state is not a deep invariant.
DelegateClass(Array)/SimpleDelegator forward the entire Array surface, push/<<, clear included, unless the mutators are undef'd; that is the leak the pattern closes.
Enumerable methods such as sort, map and sum return plain Arrays: returning them leaks the raw shape unless the domain methods wrap the result again.
